title: Pick the system that models the story
subtitle: Systems of two linear equations in two variables · 11 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **11 of the official questions in Systems of two linear equations in two variables are this one** — 7 Easy, 4 Medium, 0 Hard.
It is bottom-heavy, which makes it cheap points. Secure it early.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You get a short story with two unknown quantities, usually two kinds of item, ticket, coin or speed, and every answer choice is a pair of equations.
- The question asks which system represents the situation, not what the numbers are.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Write down what each variable stands for, including its units.
- 2) Build the 'count' equation first: the quantities add up to a total number of people, items or hours.
- 3) Build the 'value' equation: rate times quantity for each type adds up to the total money, points or distance.
- Keep only the choice with both equations right.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Mostly no help: you are matching a structure, not computing a number.
If you have already solved the story in your head, you can graph a choice to check that its intersection gives sensible whole-number values.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You swap which rate goes with which variable.
You write a 'times as many' relationship backwards, putting the multiplier on the wrong person.
Or you pick a choice whose count equation uses the money total.
With percent discounts, you might subtract the percent instead of multiplying by what is left, such as 0.8 for 20% off.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
